title: Legacy of Rescue: A Daughter's Tribute
author: Marta F. Kunecka
target_audience: Students and scholars of World War II and Jewish heritage
Individuals interested in personal family histories and memoirs
General readers seeking inspirational true stories
core_themes: Acts of courage and compassion during wartime
Intergenerational transmission of trauma and resilience
primary_purpose: To document and honor the true story of the author's father—a Hungarian Jewish survivor of the Holocaust rescued by a Polish Catholic rescuer—while reflecting on the enduring impact of this legacy on the next generation.

structure_format.organization: Chronological narrative interwoven with flashbacks, personal reflections, and historical context
features: Letters and documents as primary sources
Biographical sketches of individuals involved in the rescue

key_concepts_lessons: Individual acts of courage can save lives even amidst atrocity and violence.
Stories of rescue and survival are crucial to understanding the broader narrative of the Holocaust.
Personal and familial remembrance helps preserve the memory of both victims and rescuers.
The legacy of trauma and gratitude shapes descendants in profound ways.
Interfaith and intercultural alliances can transcend hatred, even in extreme times.
notable_features: Focuses on both personal family story and broader context
Highlights the actions of a Polish Catholic rescuer (Jozef Jarosz)
Pays tribute to Righteous Among the Nations honorees
cultural_historical_context: Set during and after World War II, primarily in Hungary and Poland, the book addresses the Holocaust, focusing on the experiences of Hungarian Jews, the role of Polish rescuers, and the post-war diaspora. Published at a time of renewed interest in Holocaust testimony and the recognition of non-Jewish rescuers by institutions like Yad Vashem.
reception_impact: Praised in Jewish and interfaith communities for its personal approach and historical value
Used as an educational tool in Holocaust and genocide studies programs
Acknowledged for bearing witness to the bravery of ordinary people during the Holocaust
Contributes to the discourse about intergenerational trauma, gratitude, and healing
comparable_titles: The Girl in the Green Sweater: A Life in Holocaust’s Shadow by Krystyna Chiger
The Lost: A Search for Six of Six Million by Daniel Mendelsohn
Defiance: The Bielski Partisans by Nechama Tec
